answerlines: Ireland (acceptEire; accept Republic ofIrelandor Poblacht na hÉireann; acceptIrishFree State;do not accept or prompt on "Northern Ireland")

clues.text: A hero from the myths of this modern country unknowingly kills his son Connla with his spear, Gae Bolg.
A story from this country, the Book of Invasions, details its mythical former residents such as the Fomorians, led by Balor, and the Tuatha Dé (TOO-huh DAY).
According to the mythology of this country, the three sisters of the Morrígan shape-shifted into crows to incite fear and panic on the battlefield.
This country’s Giant’s Causeway was created during a fight between the giant Ben-an-donner and a resident of this country.
In another myth from this country, Fionn Mac Cumhail ("Finn mac Cool") acquires all the world's knowledge.
This country's folkloreconcern Cú Chulainn, Fionn macCumhaill, and the Morrigan, a witch who is associatedwith this country's holiday of Samhain.
This country is home to the Gae Bulg-wielding Cu Chulainn as well as a man who ate the Salmon of Knowledge, Finn MacCool.
Pots of gold are hidden by folkloric creatures called leprechauns in what country from which snakes were legendarily expelled by St. Patrick?
Name this Gaelic country in the British Isles led from Dublin.
Saint Patrick legendarily drove all the snakes out of this island country.

answerlines: Ireland [or Republic of Ireland or Éire or Airlann; accept Northern Ireland]

clues.text: A character from the mythology of this country sometimes experiences a riastrad translated as “warp spasm” or “battle frenzy.”
Church bells in this country broke a 900-year curse that turned children into swans.
In one story from the mythology of this country, a man used the skin of a black sheep to heal his comrade’s wounds, after which it grew into his skin.
A woman from this country’s mythology scares a giant by having her supposedly infant son consume a griddle cake while she feeds the giant a cake with the griddle iron still inside.
Shapeshifters called púca appear in this country’s myth, as does a triple-death goddess who tricks a hero into eating dog meat.
The story about Grainne and her lover is narrated by the son of that hero from this country, the bard Oisín (“oh-SHEEN”).
The Stone of Destiny in this country sat atop the Hill of Tara.
A hero from this country sucks his thumb for wisdom after he burns it while cooking the salmon of knowledge.
Name this island home to the stories of Finn MacCool and Cu Chulainn, the latter of whom is found in its Ulster Cycle.
Name this country, whose mythology includes the hero Finn MacCool.

answerlines: Ireland [or Éire; accept Tara; accept Ulster after “Gáe Bulg” and before mentioned]

clues.text: One king of this country had his horses’ lips and tails cut out, then withstood an invasion using silent warriors revived from a cauldron.
Leaders of this region were crowned on a magical stone that would roar in joy to recognize a true king.
Three brother gods from this country are a goldsmith, carpenter, and blacksmith who work together.
This country's immram genre of magic island voyages later starred Christian monks.
A "plain of pillars" in this country was the site of a battle between the descendants of Nemed, led by Sreng, and a group whose king received a replacement silver arm after the battle.
In this region, two hounds refused to kill a deer because they recognized it was their owner’s wife.

A hero of this country betrayed a friend with a "love spot" on his head, met a deer that became his wife, and sired a bard who vanished for 300 years; that father of Ossian sleeps under this land until the hour of need, and burnt his thumb on the Salmon of Knowledge.
One hero from this region wielded a spear called the Gáe Bulg (“guy bolg”) and repelled the armies of Queen Medb (“medhv”) using an ability called riastrad during the Cattle Raid of Cooley.
Name this island whose later mythic figures would include Deirdre of the Sorrows and Cu Chulainn.
The Ulster Cycle contains stories from what home country of Cú Chulainn (“koo KULL-in”)?
